en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Fifteenth Chapter
Is it the case that "time" (addhā) is an ultimate reality (parinipphanna)?
Yes, it is.
"Is it form?
One should not say so... pe ...
"Is it feeling?"... pe ...
Is it perception?
... [and so on] ... mental formations? ...
[and so on] ... consciousness?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the past time fully established? Yes.
“Is it form?
One should not say so … pe … “Is it feeling? … pe … [One should not say so.]
Is perception … [and so on] … formations … [and so on] … consciousness?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the future time fully accomplished? Yes.
"Is it form?
One should not say so... pe ...
"Is it feeling?"... pe ...
Perception … [and so on] … volitional formations … [and so on] … consciousness?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the present time fully established? Yes.
"Is it form?
One should not say so... [and so on] ... "Is it feeling?"... [and so on] ...
Is it perception … [and so on] … volitional formations … [and so on] … consciousness?
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Is past form,
feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness the past time? Yes.
Are the five aggregates past?
You should not say so...
[and so on] ...Is future form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness the future time-period?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are the five times non-existent?
You should not say so …pe….
Is present form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness the present time?
Yes. Are there five present times? No.

It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it the case that the five past aggregates are the past time, the five future aggregates are the future time, and the five present aggregates are the present time? Yes.
"Are there fifteen times?
One should not say so...
[as before] ...Is it the case that the twelve past bases are the past time, the twelve future bases are the future time, and the twelve present bases are the present time?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there thirty-six half-months?
You should not say so… [and so on].
The eighteen elements of the past are the past time; the eighteen elements of the future are the future time; the eighteen elements of the present are the present time?
Yes. Are there thus fifty-four times?

It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that the twenty-two faculties of the past constitute the past time, the twenty-two faculties of the future constitute the future time, and the twenty-two faculties of the present constitute the present time?
Yes, it is.
“Is it sixty half-months?
One should not say so … [and so on] … It should not be said—
“Surely it is fully accomplished,” [you reply]. “Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Bhikkhus, there are these three bases for talk.
What are the three?
One might speak about the past, bhikkhus, as follows:”
‘Thus it was in the past,’ or,
monks, concerning the future time one might speak thus:
‘Thus it will be in the future.’
"Or, monks, one might speak concerning the present time thus: 'It is so now in the present.
These, monks, are the three bases for discourse."
Is it indeed a sutta?
Yes. Therefore, it must certainly be an established reality.
The Discourse on the Path is finished.
